To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the asymptotic decay of the singular values for a Weyl localization operator is governed by integrals of |μ̃ ∗ σ̃|2 and of |μ̃ ∧ σ̃|2, where μ̃ is the Fourier transform of μ, σ is the window function, and ∧ denotes convolution in the frequency domain.
the asymptotic singular value decay of any localization operator L(σ,μ) is bounded above and below by integrals involving σ and μ.
the asymptotic singular value decay rate of L(σ,μ) is bounded by integrals of |(σ ∗ μ̃)|2 and |(σ ∙ μ̃)∧ |2 outside squares of growing radius.

the asymptotics of the singular values associated to the Weyl localization operators L(σ, μ).

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the asymptotic singular value decay rate of a time-frequency localization operator can be bounded from above by the decay rate of the Gabor frame operator of the same window function.
we have developed a theory which is able to predict the singular value decay of a large class of time-frequency operators, and which can be applied in practice.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the absence of any a priori structure on Ω and μ, the asymptotic decay of the singular values is governed by the behavior of the product of μ and its Hilbert transform outside of squares.
the asymptotic singular value decay rate of L(Ω,μ) is controlled by the decay rate of μ outside Ω.
